## 3. The evidence that moved it

**A randomised controlled trial of a large language model, in October 2024.**
[39009780](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/39009780/) (*Nat Med*): outpatient reception via collaboration between
nurses and an LLM, randomised. This corpus spent 2025 recording the absence of
randomised clinical evidence for language models and building arguments on that
absence. The absence was not real.

**Pathology foundation models reach *Nature*.** [39232164](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/39232164/): a pathology
foundation model for cancer diagnosis and prognosis prediction. With
[39039250](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/39039250/) (*Nat Med*, clinical-grade computational pathology and rare-cancer
detection), the imaging branch of the foundation-model thread is publishing in
the highest-tier venues a full year before the single-cell branch attracts the
same attention.

## 4. Refutations

### (a) Landing on a tracked thread

[39465898](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/39465898/) (*NEJM*): large language models and the **degradation of the
medical record**. The harm is located in the clinical artefact rather than in
model accuracy — a different axis from every benchmark result, and the axis that
survives a model getting better. Filed as a refutation on `foundation-models`
because the thread's claim is about transfer into clinical use, and this says the
transfer damages the substrate.

### (b) Method credibility

[39333790](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/39333790/) (*Nat Comput Sci*): subtask-decomposition-based learning and
benchmarking for predicting genetic perturbation outcomes. Perturbation
prediction is the task that in June 2025 produces "simple controls exceed the
best deep learning algorithms". Here, eight months earlier, the task is already
being rebuilt around its own weaknesses — the benchmark's authors had the
objection before the null result was published.

[39443777](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/39443777/) (*Nature*): scalable watermarking for identifying LLM outputs.
Provenance infrastructure, which is what a field builds when it expects not to
be able to tell machine output from human output by inspection.
